author: project team
text: Project Iris decision: we chose a canary rollout because reversibility and a narrow blast radius mattered more than launch speed. The recorded project rationale was rollback confidence.
title: Iris rollout decision

author: SRE
text: Project Iris rollback drill restored service inside the target window while limiting impact to the canary cohort. The drill supported the rollout decision but did not author it.
title: Iris rollback drill

author: Dana Cho
text: Direct email from Dana Cho for Project Iris: for this regulated release, keep the signing key on the customer HSM because the approved module is unavailable in managed KMS. Dana explicitly says this is not a general objection to managed key services.
title: Dana regulated signing requirement

author: architecture council
text: Architecture council portfolio record: standard workloads remain approved on the centrally operated cryptographic service, and planned non-regulated workloads remain on that platform. The regulated signing exception did not alter this portfolio direction.
title: Iris portfolio cryptography strategy

author: meeting scribe
text: Project Iris meeting notes, authored by the scribe, attribute to Dana Cho: keep the migration reversible through Friday. The notes are attribution, not a direct message authored by Dana.
title: Iris migration meeting attribution

author: Dana Cho
text: Direct Project Iris email authored by Dana Cho: ship the schema change only after the replay check passes. Dana directly authored this instruction.
title: Dana replay-gate email

author: vendor
text: Vendor documentation for Project Iris says the platform can integrate with a customer HSM or a managed key service. Product capability does not define project policy or Dana Cho's general position.
title: Iris HSM capability

author: customer compliance
text: Project Iris customer residency policy requires archived customer records to remain within the EU region. The question whether an option could satisfy the rule does not require proof that production is already configured correctly.
title: Iris EU archive policy

author: vendor
text: Project Iris vendor guide states that the archive service offers an EU-only regional storage option that keeps archived records within the EU.
title: Iris EU-only archive option

author: platform
text: Project Iris deployment checklist contains an unchecked item to verify the active archive region. It does not prove that the current deployment is compliant.
title: Iris deployment checklist

author: PMO
text: Project Iris staffing note lists Dana Cho as security lead. Role proximity does not make every Iris statement directly authored by Dana.
title: Dana Cho staffing note

author: PMO
text: Project Iris release calendar lists rollout dates, migration windows, and regulated signing milestones. It records schedule, not the reasons behind policy or project decisions.
title: Iris release calendar

author: project team
text: Project Juniper decision: we raised queue capacity from 12k to 20k because month-close backlog was disrupting reconciliation. The decision records the team-owned capacity choice and rationale.
title: Juniper capacity decision

author: operations
text: Project Juniper June month-close observation: queue backlog exceeded 12k during reconciliation and drained only after the close window.
title: Juniper June close observation

author: customer security
text: Project Juniper customer policy authorizes local emergency login only during a declared identity-provider outage, requires incident commander approval, and requires a post-event audit.
title: Juniper emergency access policy

author: vendor
text: Project Juniper vendor guide says the product technically supports local emergency login. The guide describes capability and does not grant customer authorization.
title: Juniper emergency login capability

author: customer security
text: Project Juniper audit rule requires every use of the emergency login path to be reviewed in the next business-day access audit.
title: Juniper emergency audit rule

author: operations
text: Project Juniper daily spike report records a midday queue backlog unrelated to month close. It is not an independent second month-close observation.
title: Juniper daily spike

author: vendor sales
text: Project Juniper vendor sales summary calls local access flexible and easy to enable. Sales language does not override the customer's emergency-access policy.
title: Juniper vendor flexibility note

author: platform
text: Project Juniper change ticket implements queue capacity 20k after approval. It records implementation, not independent evidence that the month-close condition repeated.
title: Juniper capacity implementation

author: operations
text: Operational reconciliation archive, July cycle: at ledger cutover the work queue crossed the prior twelve-thousand ceiling again and stayed elevated until the accounting close finished. This dated archive is an independent second monthly-close observation for Project Juniper.
title: Juniper July close observation

author: operations
text: Project Juniper post-change report says the 20k queue limit prevented reconciliation backlog from reaching the new ceiling during the next close. This is later outcome evidence, not authorship of the original decision.
title: Juniper post-change report

author: finance ops
text: Project Juniper close runbook lists reconciliation owners, queue dashboards, and escalation steps for the July accounting cycle.
title: Juniper close runbook

author: vendor
text: Project Juniper vendor documentation supports queue capacities above 20k. Capability does not itself justify the team's selected capacity.
title: Juniper queue capability

author: project team
text: Project Keystone decision: we set audit-export retention to 30 days because the partner SLA required a thirty-day evidence window and the project wanted the smallest sufficient retention period.
title: Keystone 30-day retention decision

author: customer compliance
text: Project Keystone customer policy requires audit exports to be retained for at least 30 days. The policy is the governing external retention requirement at this stage.
title: Keystone original retention policy

author: vendor
text: Project Keystone vendor guide says the export archive technically supports 90-day retention. Vendor capability does not itself change the customer's governing retention requirement.
title: Keystone 90-day capability

author: platform
text: Project Keystone storage configuration was set to 30-day audit-export retention after the project decision.
title: Keystone 30-day implementation

author: meeting scribe
text: Project Keystone partner meeting notes say the thirty-day evidence window matched the then-current SLA. The notes do not supersede customer policy.
title: Keystone partner meeting

author: analytics
text: Project Keystone cache layer uses a 30-day analytics TTL for temporary reporting data. This is unrelated to audit-export retention.
title: Keystone unrelated cache TTL

author: audit
text: Project Keystone audit report verified that the configured audit-export retention met the then-current 30-day customer requirement.
title: Keystone retention audit

author: PMO
text: Project Keystone roadmap discusses future archive changes but does not authorize a retention period different from current customer policy.
title: Keystone archive roadmap

author: customer compliance
text: Project Keystone customer compliance addendum supersedes the earlier retention requirement: audit exports must now be retained for at least 90 days, effective immediately. The earlier 30-day policy is no longer current.
title: Keystone 90-day policy addendum

author: project team
text: Project Keystone superseding decision: we changed audit-export retention from 30 days to 90 days to comply with the new customer addendum. This decision explicitly supersedes the prior 30-day project decision.
title: Keystone superseding retention decision

author: platform
text: Project Keystone change ticket updates audit-export retention to 90 days after the new policy and superseding decision.
title: Keystone 90-day implementation

author: customer compliance
text: Project Keystone correction note states that references to 30-day audit-export retention are historical after the effective 90-day customer requirement. The correction does not apply to the separate analytics cache TTL.
title: Keystone retention correction note
